name: SCFA-Acetate
notes: Union of all genes across Acetate-1, Acetate-2, and Acetate-3 pathways. Summary rule pointing to three acetate production routes.

name: SCFA-Propionate
notes: Union of all genes across Propionate-1 (methylmalonyl-CoA), Propionate-2 (acrylate/lactate), and Propionate-3 (propionyl-CoA) routes.

name: SCFA-Butyrate
notes: Union of all genes across Butyrate-1 (acetyl-CoA condensation), Butyrate-2 (glutarate), Butyrate-3 (lysine), and Butyrate-4 (4-aminobutyrate) routes.

name: SCFA-Lactate
notes: Union of all genes across Lactate-1, Lactate-2, and Lactate-3 routes. Summarizes L-lactate and D-lactate production capacity.

name: Hydrogenotrophic Methanogen
notes: For a genome to have hydrogneotrophic methanogenesis potential, it must encode mcrA, at least 4 genes of the methyl branch of the Wood-lungdahl pathway,  part of the MTR complex, and at least one gene for any known hydrgenotrophic hdyrogenase.

name: Acetoclastic Methanogen
notes: For a genome to have acetoclastic methanogenesis potential, it must encode mcrA, part of the ACS_CODH complex, and either Acetate Kinase and Phosphotransacetylase OR Acetyl CoA Synthetase. There is a MANDATORY taxonomic requirement for this rule to run, and a MAG or genome must also belong to the genus Methanosarcina or the family Methanotrichaceae

name: Methylotrophic Methanogen
notes: For a genome to have methyltotrophic methanogenesis potential, it must encode mcrA and at least one substrate-demethylating corrinoid-dependent methyltransferase homolog "MtxB"

name: Hydrogen Metabolism
notes: HMM-based annotation only. No KEGG K-numbers available for NiFe and FeFe hydrogenase groups; all detection relies on HMM profiles in DRAM2 (NiFe_group1‚Äö√Ñ√¨4, FeFe_GroupA/B/C/E/F). gene_ids intentionally left blank.

name: Oxygen - Low Affinity Use
notes: Low affinity oxygen use indicates an aerobe and requires the presence of a low-affinity oxidase plus a majority of the elctron transport chain

name: Oxygen - High Affinity Use
notes: High affinity oxygen use indicates a microaerophile and requires the presence of a high-affinity oxidase plus a majority of the elctron transport chain

name: Nitrate Reduction To Nitrite
notes: Nitrate reduction to nitrite can occur through either the membrane-bound Nar system (K00370, K00371) or the periplasmic Nap system (K02567, K02568). Either system completes the nitrate transformation step.

notes: The reduction of nitrous oxide (N‚Äö√á√áO) to dinitrogen gas (N‚Äö√á√á) is catalyzed by nitrous oxide reductase (nosZ, K00376). Presence of this gene indicates the potential for the final step of denitrification, converting greenhouse gas N‚Äö√á√áO into inert atmospheric N‚Äö√á√á.

name: Sulfate Reduction
notes: A genome that encodes adenylysulfate reductase and dissimilatory sulfite reductase

name: Tetrathionate Reduction
notes: Tetrathionate reductase complex (ttrABC): TtrA catalytic subunit (K08359), TtrB electron transfer subunit (K08358), TtrC membrane anchor (K08357). At least 2 of 3 subunits required to allow for incomplete genome recovery. Tetrathionate is generated in the inflamed gut from host-derived thiosulfate oxidation and is exploited as an electron acceptor by Salmonella enterica and other Enterobacteriaceae during inflammation, conferring a growth advantage. Rule mirrors Thiosulfate Reduction group ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ both are non-sulfate sulfur respiration pathways enriched during gut dysbiosis.

name: Fumarate Respiration
notes: Presence of both succinate dehydrogenase (K00239‚Äö√Ñ√¨K00242) and fumarate reductase (K00244‚Äö√Ñ√¨K00247) indicates capacity for fumarate respiration, in which fumarate and succinate are interconverted via membrane-bound electron transport complexes. This allows microbes to use fumarate as an electron acceptor or to oxidize succinate as part of a truncated TCA/respiratory chain, a process that can act as a succinate-consuming pathway in the gut and influence luminal succinate levels and host responses

name: TMAO Reduction
notes: TMAO reductase systems: TorA (K03532) or TorZ/BisZ (K07811) catalytic subunit paired with TorC (K03533) or TorY/BisC (K07821) cytochrome c subunit. Either complete reductase system (TorAC or TorZY) indicates anaerobic TMAO respiration capacity. TMAO is an abundant dietary-derived compound in fish and meat; gut Enterobacteriaceae reduce it to TMA, which is subsequently oxidized by the host liver to TMAO ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ connecting microbial metabolism to host cardiovascular risk.

name: Quorum Sensing
notes: Quorum sensing via three systems: (1) AHL/LuxI-LuxR: LuxI-type AHL synthases lasI (K13060) or rhlI/cepI/tofI homologs (K13061) paired with LuxR-type receptors lasR (K18304) or rhlR homologs (K18099) ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ both synthase and receptor required; (2) AI-2/LuxS system: LuxS S-ribosylhomocysteine lyase (K07173) ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ widely conserved but interpret alone cautiously as it has metabolic roles beyond QS; (3) AI-2 import via Lsr ABC transporter: LsrB substrate-binding (K10555), LsrC permease (K10556), LsrD permease (K10557), LsrA ATPase (K10558) ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ at least 2 subunits required ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ indicates active AI-2 uptake and response capacity.

name: Motility
notes: Flagellar motor (MotA K02410 or MotB K02411; at least one required) plus at least 3 structural/assembly genes from the flagellar complex. Required for surface approach and early biofilm attachment. Also relevant for chemotaxis toward carbon/electron donor sources in engineered systems.

name: Bile Acid Deconjugation
notes: Presence of choloylglycine hydrolase (K01442), the canonical bile salt hydrolase (BSH), indicates capacity to deconjugate glycine- and taurine-conjugated bile acids to free bile acids and amino acids

Genomes satisfying this rule are high-confidence secondary bile acid producers capable of converting primary bile acids (e.g., cholic acid, chenodeoxycholic acid) into secondary bile acids (e.g., deoxycholic acid, lithocholic acid) in the human gut

name: Bile Acid Redox
notes: Presence of at least one bile acid‚Äö√Ñ√¨active hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase indicates capacity to oxidize and epimerize bile acids at the 3 or 7 positions via oxo intermediates. These enzymes are essential for forming iso‚Äö√Ñ√´ and urso‚Äö√Ñ√´bile acids and for completing epi‚Äö√Ñ√´bile acid pathways in the human gut

name: Menaquinone (K2)
notes: Co-occurrence of menF (K02552), menD (K02551), menC (K02549), menB (K01661), menE (K01911), and menA (K02548) represents the full classical menaquinone biosynthesis pathway from chorismate to polyprenylated menaquinone

name: Folate
notes: Co-occurrence of dihydropteroate synthase (K00796) and dihydrofolate reductase (K00287) marks the minimal two-step folate synthesis/recycling module from p-aminobenzoate to tetrahydrofolate. Folate-prototrophic gut microbes (Lactobacillus reuteri, Bifidobacterium spp.) supply folate to the host and folate-auxotrophic microbiome members, supporting one-carbon metabolism and nucleotide synthesis.

name: Thiamine
notes: Co-occurrence of thiamine-phosphate pyrophosphorylase (K03147/ThiE) and hydroxyethylthiazole kinase (K00788/ThiM) marks the minimal thiamine biosynthesis completion module. Thiamine-producing gut microbes contribute to host B1 supply and support TPP-dependent metabolic pathways in the microbiome. Full de novo synthesis requires additional ThiC/ThiG upstream enzymes not captured here; this rule flags thiamine phosphate assembly capacity.

name: Biotin (B7)
notes: Biotin synthase (K01012/BioB) catalyzes the final step of biotin biosynthesis, inserting a sulfur atom into dethiobiotin to form biotin (vitamin B7). Presence alone indicates biotin biosynthesis completion capacity. Biotin-prototrophic gut microbes (Fusobacterium nucleatum, some Bacteroides) contribute to colonic biotin supply; biotin is essential for carboxylase enzymes including pyruvate carboxylase and acetyl-CoA carboxylase.

name: Niacin (B3)
notes: Co-occurrence of aspartate oxidase (K03517/NadB), quinolinate synthase (K00278/NadA), and nicotinate-nucleotide pyrophosphorylase (K00767/NadC) marks the de novo NAD biosynthesis route from aspartate through quinolinate. Niacin/B3-prototrophic gut microbes produce nicotinamide and support luminal NAD+ precursor availability, relevant for host intestinal epithelial function and microbiome-host signaling via extracellular NAD+ metabolites.

name: Cobalamin (B12)
notes: Presence of all core corrinoid loop assembly genes in KEGG module M00122 (cobyrinate a,c-diamide ‚Äö√ú√≠ cobalamin), with allowed alternatives at specific steps, indicates capacity for de novo completion of cobalamin (vitamin B12) biosynthesis. This marks high-confidence B12 producers in gut and rumen microbiomes, which can support cobalamin-dependent pathways in both microbes and the host.

name: Pantothenate (B5)
notes: Presence of all core pantothenate biosynthesis genes from either the valine/aspartate route (M00119) or the 2‚Äö√Ñ√´oxoisovalerate/spermine route (M00913) indicates de novo vitamin B5 production capacity.

name: Pyridoxine (B6)
notes: Presence of all core genes in KEGG module M00124 (erythrose-4P ‚Äö√ú√≠ pyridoxal 5'-phosphate) indicates capacity for de novo vitamin B6 biosynthesis as PLP. In gut and rumen microbiomes, such B6 prototrophy is less prevalent than other B-vitamin pathways but supports amino acid metabolism and can provide B6 to auxotrophic microbes and the host

name: Riboflavin (B2)
notes: Presence of all core genes in KEGG module M00125 (riboflavin biosynthesis, GTP ‚Äö√ú√≠ riboflavin/FM N/FAD) with allowed enzyme alternatives indicates capacity for de novo vitamin B2 biosynthesis. In gut and rumen microbiomes, such riboflavin prototrophy is an important microbial trait that supplies B2 for FMN/FAD cofactor production and can contribute to host vitamin status

name: Tma Production
notes: TMA production via three routes: (1) choline TMA-lyase complex cutC/cutD (K20038/K20037) ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ primary choline-to-TMA route; (2) carnitine oxygenase cntA (K22443) ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ L-carnitine cleavage; (3) glycine reductase grdH (K21579) ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ glycine betaine reduction. TMA is the gut microbial precursor of host-produced TMAO, a circulating metabolite associated with cardiovascular disease risk. All three routes are diet-substrate-dependent.

name: Tma Demethylation
notes: TMA demethylation via pyrrolysine-containing methyltransferases: MttB-type trimethylamine methyltransferase (K14083), MtgB glycine betaine methyltransferase (K25600), or EC:2.1.1.389 (dimethylamine/trimethylamine corrinoid methyltransferase). Removes a methyl group from TMA, reducing circulating TMA and potentially TMAO levels. Found in Methanomassiliicoccales archaea and some anaerobic bacteria. NOTE: EC:2.1.1.389 is not yet a KEGG K-number ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ confirm DRAM2 can accept EC:identifiers in rule engine.

name: Beta-Lactam Resistance
notes: Beta-lactamase and penicillin-binding protein resistance genes conferring resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics (penicillins, cephalosporins, carbapenems). Major antibiotic resistance gene class in environmental microbiomes.

name: Macrolide Resistance
notes: Macrolide resistance via efflux pumps, ribosomal methylases (erm genes), or macrolide esterases.

name: Tetracycline Resistance
notes: Tetracycline resistance via efflux pumps (tet efflux genes) or ribosomal protection proteins.

name: Sulfonamide Resistance
notes: Sulfonamide resistance via dihydropteroate synthase variants (sul1, sul2, sul3) insensitive to sulfonamide inhibition. Sulfonamide resistance genes are among the most prevalent antibiotic resistance determinants in human gut microbiomes, particularly in individuals with prior antibiotic exposure, and are frequently found on mobile genetic elements that co-carry other resistance genes.

name: Aminoglycoside Resistance
notes: Presence of aminoglycoside-modifying enzyme genes, including N-acetyltransferases (AAC(3), AAC(6‚Äö√Ñ‚â§)), O-nucleotidyltransferases (aadA, ANT(3¬†‚à´); K00984), and O-phosphotransferases (APH(3‚Äö√Ñ‚â§), APH(3¬†‚à´)), indicates resistance to aminoglycoside antibiotics via drug inactivation. Aminoglycoside resistance genes of these families are common in human and animal gut microbiomes and in the rumen, where they contribute substantially to the overall resistome

name: Glycopeptide Resistance
notes: Presence of all core genes in KEGG module M00651, encoding the D-Ala‚Äö√Ñ√¨D-Lac type vancomycin resistance cluster, indicates capacity to replace the D-Ala‚Äö√Ñ√¨D-Ala terminus of peptidoglycan precursors with D-Ala‚Äö√Ñ√¨D-Lac and thereby reduce vancomycin binding. This mechanism is characteristic of vancomycin-resistant enterococci and other glycopeptide-resistant Gram-positive bacteria and can occur in gut and rumen microbiomes as part of the glycopeptide resistome

name: Prodrug Activation
notes: Prodrug activation: azoreductase (K01118) reduces azo-bond prodrugs (sulfasalazine, balsalazide) to release active 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) in the colon. Primary enzymatic mechanism by which IBD prodrugs are activated by gut microbiota. Presence indicates capacity to convert prodrugs to their active forms, with implications for inter-individual variation in drug response.

name: Chemotherapy Inactivation
notes: Chemotherapy inactivation: co-occurrence of cytosine deaminase (K17722) and uracil phosphoribosyltransferase (K17723) encodes the 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) inactivation pathway. Gut microbes expressing these enzymes can degrade 5-FU to inactive catabolites, potentially reducing drug efficacy. Relevant to colorectal cancer chemotherapy outcomes where microbiome composition affects 5-FU bioavailability.

name: Nitro Drug Reduction
notes: Nitro drug reduction: nitroreductase type I (K10678) or type II (K10679) reduces nitro groups in prodrugs such as metronidazole, nitrofurantoin, and tinidazole. Reductive activation converts these prodrugs to toxic intermediates that damage DNA. Paradoxically, acquired resistance in Helicobacter pylori and Bacteroides involves loss or mutation of these reductases ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ flagging presence indicates susceptibility to nitro-drug activation.

name: Neurological Drugs
notes: Levodopa decarboxylase / aromatic amino acid decarboxylase (K22330/TyrDC) decarboxylates L-DOPA to dopamine in the gut lumen. Gut microbial DOPA decarboxylation reduces levodopa bioavailability and is a key mechanism underlying inter-individual variation in Parkinson's disease treatment efficacy. Inhibiting gut microbial K22330 activity is an active therapeutic target.

name: Urease
notes: Urea hydrolysis requires the full urease enzyme complex composed of subunits ureC (K01428), ureB (K01429), and ureA (K01430). All three subunits are required for activity. In the gut, urease-positive organisms (Helicobacter pylori, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus mirabilis) hydrolyze urea to ammonia and CO‚Äö√á√á, raising local pH and supporting colonization of acidic niches. In the rumen, urease activity by diverse Firmicutes and Proteobacteria is central to urea nitrogen recycling and represents a major route by which dietary or salivary urea re-enters the microbial nitrogen pool

name: Iron Acquisition
notes: Siderophore receptors (K19611/fepA, K16090/fiu, K16091/fecA), heme acquisition (K12545/hasA, K16152/hasR), siderophore/yersiniabactin receptors (K15721/fyuA), and iron complex TonB-dependent receptors (K16088, K16089, K16087, K02014). Broad outer-membrane iron uptake capacity.

name: Hemolysins
notes: Pore-forming hemolysins: HlyA (K11005), HlyII (K11032), leukocidin/Hlg family (K11038), and HlyC-family protein (K06189). Note: K06189 and K11005/K11032/K11038 are also present in Toxins row ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ expected overlap between hemolysin and toxin categories.

name: Pilus And Fimbrial Adhesion
notes: Surface attachment to gut epithelium via fimbrial and pilus systems.

name: Epithelial Invasion
notes: Active invasion of gut epithelial cells via multiple mechanisms.

name: Type Iii Secretion System
notes: Type III secretion system capacity via structural components or secreted effectors

name: Type Vi Secretion System
notes: Type VI secretion system capacity via Hcp tube proteins or VgrG spike proteins.

name: Iga Protease
notes: IgA1 protease (K01347) cleaves human immunoglobulin IgA1 at the hinge region, inactivating mucosal antibody defense. Produced by Neisseria, Haemophilus, and Streptococcus pneumoniae as a major immune evasion strategy in mucosal pathogens. In the gut, IgA protease activity can disrupt the secretory IgA coat that normally excludes commensal and pathogenic bacteria from the epithelium.

name: Toxins
notes: Covers genotoxins (CDT K11014, colibactin K26579), pore-forming/hemolysins (K06189, K11005, K11032, K11038), ER stress (subtilase K19297/K19298), vacuolating (VacA K11028), heat-labile enterotoxin complex (K10928+K10929), heat-stable enterotoxin (K16883/K16884), Shiga toxin (K11006/K11007)
